newsitem.title: USA: U.S. energy prices higher on ACCESS, sell-off seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. energy prices higher on ACCESS, sell-off seen.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices stayed firm several hours into after-hours trade, but traders forecast technical weakness for early Wednesday.
"We're still looking for crude to test $23.40 a barrel," before resuming a rally, said one ACCESS trader.
American Petroleum Institute, an industry trade group, reported distillate inventories fell 17,000 barrels to 112.3 million, leaving them 18.7 million below year-ago levels.
November heating oil climbed 0.84 cent to 71.60 cents by 2210 EDT/2610 GMT on ACCESS.
November crude oil traded 24 cents higher at $24.38 a barrel.

Front-month unleaded gasoline followed "heat's" lead, bucking a build of 2.27 million barrels. November gasoline rose as high as 63.40 on ACCESS, then eased to 63 cents -- a 0.18 cent advantage from the settlement.
Traders and brokers saw consolidation in gasoline on Wednesday, pressured by the bearish API data.
But heating oil would stay firm, they said, with major support at 79.10 cents.
